recent_posts.title: Tracking AI-generated code in production
recent_posts.summary: Git AI is a tool that hooks into AI coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot) to attribute which lines of code were AI-written, storing that metadata in Git Notes and tracking it through to production. Key features include an `ai blame` command to trace lines back to their original prompt and agent session, and a team dashboard showing AI usage per developer and repo over time. The author raises an open question about whether this kind of observability genuinely improves engineering decisions around hiring, code review, and risk, or simply adds overhead.

recent_posts.title: Do you miss the ability to write scripts in api tools in python?
recent_posts.summary: Most API tools like Postman and Insomnia restrict pre/post-request scripting to JavaScript only, forcing developers whose primary language is Python to context-switch even when their entire backend or automation stack is Python-based. This creates friction for tasks like auth signing, request chaining, and response processing. The post raises the question of whether multi-language scripting support in API tools would improve developer productivity and workflow consistency.

recent_posts.title: Project Nylo : A Privacy-first cross-domain analytics without cookies or fingerprinting
recent_posts.summary: Project Nylo introduces WTX-1, an open protocol for privacy-first cross-domain analytics that avoids cookies and fingerprinting. It uses pseudonymous random identifiers (WaiTags) passed via URL hash fragments, which are never transmitted to servers per RFC 3986. Tokens are HMAC-signed, short-lived, one-time-use, and destination domains must be pre-authorized via DNS TXT records. The protocol includes a Consent API with anonymous fallback mode. The author is seeking community feedback on security, GDPR compliance, browser vendor compatibility, and protocol design ahead of potential standardization.

recent_posts.title: When One Line of Code Works Everywhere - Except Behind CloudFront
recent_posts.summary: A production Next.js app worked identically on two AWS deployments but broke on a third when CloudFront was added. The CDN stripped React Server Components headers, causing router.replace() to trigger full page reloads instead of lightweight updates, destroying Redux state mid-API-call. The fix decoupled navigation from API calls by moving logic to Redux thunks and using window.history.replaceState() instead of Next.js router methods. The incident reveals how CDNs and proxies can silently break framework protocols that depend on specific HTTP headers passing through infrastructure layers.

recent_posts.title: Reading Between the Lines: Postman Changes and What Devs Value
recent_posts.summary: Developer sentiment around Postman's recent changes reveals core priorities: git-native workflows, local-first architecture, reliable import capabilities, speed over features, seamless secrets management, and selective automation. The underlying issue isn't feature competition but trust—developers want tools that respect their existing workflows rather than forcing cloud-only, proprietary solutions. Key pain points include vendor lock-in concerns, friction from cloud-dependent tools, and the need for smooth integration with environment variables and secret managers.

recent_posts.title: Revolutionizing Geolocation: The New <geolocation> HTML Element in Chrome 144
recent_posts.summary: Chrome 144 introduces a new `<geolocation>` HTML element that simplifies location access through a declarative, user-initiated button instead of imperative JavaScript calls. The element handles permissions and data retrieval automatically, reducing boilerplate code while improving success rates by 20-54% in real-world trials. Key features include attributes for auto-location, accuracy modes, and continuous updates, plus built-in styling constraints to prevent deception. Developers can access position data through events and properties, with automatic fallback support for older browsers through polyfills.

recent_posts.title: “Overqualified” – 6-month update from inside the same company
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their 6-month journey after being labeled 'overqualified' during an internal application. They transitioned to a Junior IT Engineer role within the same company, handling day-to-day tasks like printer support, DHCP management, and internal tools while building a POS-lite side project using Java, Spring Boot, and React. The update reflects on navigating career pivots, dealing with workplace labels, and finding better role alignment.

recent_posts.title: express-error-toolkit — One Package to Handle All Express Errors
recent_posts.summary: A new NPM package that consolidates common Express error handling patterns into a single toolkit. It provides pre-built middleware for global error handling and 404 routes, type-safe custom error classes, an async handler utility to avoid try-catch blocks, and colorful console logging. The package supports both CommonJS and ESM, offers configuration through environment variables, and aims to eliminate repetitive boilerplate code across Express projects.

recent_posts.title: From searching to solving: how Vector Databases transform product discovery
recent_posts.summary: Semantic search enables users to find products by describing their needs in natural language rather than exact keywords. A practical demo built with LangChain.js and Ollama demonstrates how vector databases and embeddings power intent-based search locally without requiring API keys, transforming product discovery from keyword matching to understanding user intent.

recent_posts.title: Powerful Open-Source Webcam Tester Library
recent_posts.summary: An open-source library that pre-tests webcam and microphone functionality before users enter video applications. It validates permissions, device enumeration and selection, resolution capabilities from 144p to 4K, and lighting conditions. The library integrates with React, Vue, vanilla JavaScript, or via CDN with minimal setup time.

top_posts.title: I Built a Terminal-Based Portfolio You Can Access via SSH
top_posts.summary: A developer created an innovative terminal-based portfolio accessible via SSH using React Ink for the UI and a custom Go SSH server. The project combines React components with terminal interfaces, allowing users to explore a portfolio directly from their command line without needing a browser. The setup runs on a VPS and demonstrates creative ways to showcase developer work by meeting developers in their native environment.

top_posts.title: Static is boring — animate your icons 🎯
top_posts.summary: AnimateIcons is a React library that transforms static SVG icons into smooth animations. It offers 45+ animated icons, works with React and Next.js, supports hover and programmatic control, and integrates with ShadCN CLI. The library aims to enhance user interfaces by adding purposeful motion to icons.

top_posts.title: I built an API for my darkest moments (and yours too)
top_posts.summary: A developer created StayStrong, a simple Express.js REST API that serves over 500 motivational messages in English and Italian to help people during difficult times. The API features rate limiting, uses JSON files for data storage, and was born from personal experience with mental health struggles. The project aims to provide virtual support and encouragement to anyone who needs it.

top_posts.title: RegexBuilder - Build Regex Visually
top_posts.summary: RegexBuilder is a user-friendly tool for creating complex regular expressions visually, making the process simpler and more efficient.
